I'm really into linguistics and learn languages for a hobby (fairly competent in French, German, and Spanish at this point. Have also done basics in Portuguese, Italian, Latin, and even Czech and Russian).

Objectively it's immersion but that's not realistic for most people and I've never used that method anyway.

Duolingo is good as an intro to grammar in other languages. A useful tool, but word if warning that it's pozzed to all hell. All the cartoon people they have talking in the sentences are sand niggers, and if you go through their "stories" section it's filled with sodomite characters. But if you can look past that and just focus on the actual language instruction, you will learn. But it only gets you see far.

Spaced repetition software is extremely useful for vocab. I generally use Memrise for that, plenty of free courses on there in target languages. Anki is a similar website that has good reviews.

Lately what I've been using to take my comprehension to the next level is a site called Clozemaster, where you fill in blank words into sentences using contextual cues. It really helps with getting the verb forms down pat - using the correct form naturally in a sentence without having to stop and think about conjugation charts and shit.

Finally, it's helpful to consume media in your target languages. You can find music or videos about just about anything on YouTube. Audio tracks on movies or tv shows can often be changed to different languages and/or you can use subtitles. Finally you can get books to read - one that is free and easy to find online in every language on earth is the Bible. Practice with reading in your target language and English side by side to make sense of how sentences are formed, etc.
